Robot or PC IPs, comma-separated, like ROS_STATIC_PEERS. Use it when topics don\'t show up: many Wi-Fi networks drop multicast.
ip or ip:port (11811 by default), like ROS_DISCOVERY_SERVER. For large networks, 4G or VPN: the robot must use the same server.
tcp/ip:7447. For robots that use rmw_zenoh_cpp: the app connects to their Zenoh router (ros2 run rmw_zenoh_cpp rmw_zenohd) instead of DDS.
Use either foxglove_bridge or Zenoh, not both
How service calls (and actions, parameters, lifecycle) are packed. Automatic picks Fast DDS or Cyclone DDS for each service from its server. Change it only if services do not answer.

ws://ip:8765. When set, the app connects to that bridge by WebSocket instead of DDS: it works over the internet or mobile data. Services and parameters work through it too; actions need the bridge started with include_hidden:=true.
Comma-separated IPs or names, e.g. wlan0. Empty = all.

RViz and the everyday ROS 2 tools, in your pocket. Here are the basics in under a minute.
In Config, set the same ROS_DOMAIN_ID as your robot. If topics don\'t show up, add the robot\'s IP under Discovery peers and run Network check. Robots you\'ve seen are remembered for next time.
Tap + to add tabs: 3D view, cameras, teleop, buttons, diagnostics… or build a Dashboard with several of them on one screen. Long-press a tab to rename or delete it.
Drive with the joystick or a gamepad, make buttons that call services or send goals, and configure or activate lifecycle nodes.
List nodes, topics, services and actions, see how they connect in the node graph and browse the TF tree. Edit parameters, echo topics and call services, like the ros2 CLI.
Record topics to MCAP and play them back. Turn on alerts in Config to get notified when something goes wrong.
Save everything as a robot profile: it syncs with your account, and you can export it to a file or share it with a QR code.
Demo mode runs a simulated robot on this phone. Drive it and watch it in RViz, without touching your real network.
3D view of your robot: TF, maps, lasers, point clouds, markers…
The same displays as RViz: Grid, TF, RobotModel, Map, LaserScan, PointCloud2, Path, Pose, Odometry, Markers and more.
Orbit, top-down, first person and follow views.
Send Nav2 goals and initial poses by dragging on the floor.
Live image from any camera topic.
Finds the image topics on the network for you.
Shows resolution, encoding and frame rate.
Drive the robot with an on-screen joystick.
Publishes geometry_msgs/Twist (or TwistStamped) at a steady rate.
Speed limits, presets and axis inversion.
Safety stop if the network, the gamepad or the app stops responding.
Works with a physical gamepad too.
Two joysticks: for holonomic robots and drones.
Left stick moves, right stick turns (or any mapping you choose).
Same safety stop and limits as the single joystick.
Your own buttons that publish, call services or send action goals.
A grid of buttons, each with its own message, request or goal.
Hold-to-repeat publishing, confirmation before sending and colors.
Feedback and result of actions, with cancel.
Sliders that publish a number: a speed, an angle, a brightness, a setpoint…
Each slider moves one numeric field of any message (std_msgs/Float64 data, Twist linear.x…); the other fields keep fixed values.
Publishes while you drag (at the rate you choose) or only when you let go. Tap the value to type an exact one.
Optionally springs back to its initial value when released, and never keeps publishing when the tab is hidden.
Numbers, gauges, bars, lights and tables with live values from any topic.
Each indicator shows one field of any message (a battery level, a temperature, a mode, a flag…), or every field in a table.
Gauges and bars go from a minimum to a maximum; a light turns on when the value is true or crosses a threshold.
Marks the values as stale when the topic stops publishing. Works great as dashboard widgets.
Plots: several panels, series from any topic, XY plots and bags.
Up to 3 panels share the time axis: pinch to zoom in time, drag to go back and tap to see every value at that instant.
Each series is a numeric field of any message, with derivative, moving average, scale and offset. A panel can show x against y (a trajectory).
Open a recorded MCAP bag to plot it whole with a timeline, without publishing anything, and export everything to CSV.
Your robot on a street map, from a GPS (sensor_msgs/NavSatFix).
Shows the position, its accuracy circle and the track on OpenStreetMap maps.
Follows the robot, or move and zoom the map freely. Shows latitude, longitude, altitude and the fix type.
Watch a behavior tree run live, like Groot2: which node is running, what succeeded and what failed.
Connects to a BehaviorTree.CPP 4 Groot2Publisher (port 1667): the full tree, subtrees included, with the state of every node.
Or listens to Nav2\'s /behavior_tree_log. Tap a node for its ports; tap a SubTree to fold it.
The latest message of any topic as a tree you can unfold.
Write a path to see only part of it: pose.position, poses[-1], status{name==motor}.
Rate and age of the messages; pause it, or copy what you see as JSON.
The parameters of a node, at hand to change them.
Pick a node on the network: its parameters with their types, ranges and descriptions.
Tap one to change it. Add it to a dashboard next to the plots to tune a controller.
Logs, /diagnostics, topic echo and live plots.
Log: /rosout with level and text filters, like rqt_console.
Diagnostics: grouped by level, like rqt_robot_monitor.
Echo and Plot: any topic, with numeric fields plotted live.
See and change the state of managed (lifecycle) nodes.
Finds lifecycle nodes on the network.
Live state of each node and buttons for the transitions it allows: configure, activate, deactivate, cleanup and shutdown.
Every node on the network, with its parameters.
Like ros2 node list. Tap a node to see and edit its parameters,
and what it publishes, subscribes to and the services it offers.
Every topic, with live echo and rate.
Like ros2 topic list. Tap a topic to see its last message, its rate (Hz) and who publishes and subscribes to it.
Every service, and call any of them.
Like ros2 service list. Tap a service to fill in a request and see the response.
Every action, and send goals with live feedback.
Like ros2 action list. Tap an action to send a goal, follow its feedback and cancel it.
Record topics to MCAP and play them back.
Play back at 0.5×, 1× or 2×, in a loop.
Share recordings or import bags recorded on the robot.
